analysis.title: Bath & Body Works Inc. (BBWI) 3Q26 Recap: Underlying business trends remain pressured; tariffs and oil costs to weigh on 4Q gross margins
key_insights: BBWI closed up +1.3% (vs. the S&P down -2.0%) after its 3Q beat and FY26 top-line guidance raise. 4Q guidance came in at the low end of expectations on the top line and below expectations on the bottom line.

GS reiterates Sell with a 12-month price target of $20 (vs. $19 prior), 5.8% upside to the $18.91 price. GS says the company is in an investment year, the underlying business remains under pressure, and it is too early to call an inflection. GS does not expect a return to growth this year.
3Q sales were $1,577mn against FactSet consensus of $1,551mn, a -1.1% y/y decline. That is an improvement from the -2.3% decline in 2Q.
Store traffic stayed a headwind in 3Q, particularly late in the quarter, as inflation weighed on consumers and competition in core categories intensified.

Body care (~37% of FY25 North America sales) came in well below management expectations, with HSD sales declines roughly consistent with 2Q. Management blamed weak Halloween and seasonal products and said body care is the most competitive category.

Soaps and sanitizers grew LSD, led by sanitizers. Home fragrance was roughly flat, with single and four-wick candles, Wallflowers and concentrated room sprays growing, offset by a decline in Halloween seasonal products.

New franchises are getting a positive response. Over 50% of Essentials customers (launched Sept '26) returned within 30 days. Everyday Luxuries retail sales doubled vs. the same period last year. The Reserve four-wick candle (launched Aug '26) is achieving repeat purchases above the company benchmark.
Management said it increased marketing spend, including celebrity partnerships, and saw improving trends from new, existing and reactivated customers, particularly in digital.

Ulta and Amazon channels gained momentum. BBWI will expand to ~1,500 Ulta stores (from ~600) and launch Pink Suede exclusively there. Amazon data shows BBWI winning back lost share, with a materially higher AUR than its own channels. Both channels are expected to grow sequentially in 4Q.

4Q net sales guidance is -5.5% to -2.0% (consensus -2.1%), a sequential worsening on a smaller wholesale lift and a pressured consumer. The high end implies North America retail sales roughly flat in 4Q vs. 3Q.
4Q gross margin faces pressure from incremental Canadian tariffs (over 100bps), higher crude oil costs (~100bps), and buying and occupancy deleverage on lower sales and real estate investment.

GS cut its 4Q26 gross margin estimate to 42.2% from 44.3% and its 4Q26 EPS estimate to $1.48 from $1.70. FY26 EPS goes to $2.67 from $2.73 (-2.5%), and FY27/FY28 EPS rise 3.5%/3.6% to $2.69/$2.95. GS introduces an FY29 EPS estimate of $3.23. The FY26 numbers include the $80mn tariff refund received in 2Q26.

The price target methodology uses a lower market multiple of 17.6x (vs. 22.6x prior) and higher downside/base/upside relative P/E multiples of 35%/40%/45% (vs. 25%/30%/35%). GS says this reflects less downside risk as the company progresses on its Consumer First Formula strategy.
GS risk-reward: downside $13 (-31%, 25% probability), base $20 (+6%, 50%), upside $27 (+45%, 25%). The probability-weighted average is $20.
At $18.91, BBWI trades at 7.1x FY26E P/E and 5.4x EV/EBITDA, with a 16.4% FCF yield and a 4.2% dividend yield on GS estimates. Net debt/EBITDA is 2.2x in FY26E.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Sell and raises the target to $20 from $19. The underlying business is under pressure, traffic is weak, body care is soft, and 4Q guidance is weak on the top line and the bottom line.

earnings_insights: BBWI 3Q26 net sales reported at $1,577mn vs. FactSet consensus of $1,551mn, -1.1% y/y (2Q was -2.3%). The company beat on 3Q and raised FY26 top-line guidance.
4Q26 net sales guidance of -5.5% to -2.0% y/y vs. consensus of -2.1%, which is the low end on the top line. Bottom-line 4Q guidance is below expectations.
4Q26 gross margin pressure: incremental Canadian tariffs (over 100bps), crude oil (~100bps), and buying and occupancy deleverage.
GS estimates (not reported): 4Q26E adj. EPS $1.48 (old $1.70), net sales $2,609.3mn (old $2,639.9mn, -4.2% y/y), gross margin 42.2% (old 44.3%), EBIT $447.0mn (old $515.3mn).

GS estimates (not reported): FY26E adj. EPS $2.67 (old $2.73), FY27E $2.69 (old $2.60), FY28E $2.95 (old $2.85), FY29E $3.23. FY26E net sales are $7,078.3mn (-2.9% y/y). The FY26 estimate includes the $80mn tariff refund received in 2Q26.
GS quarterly EPS estimates (not reported): 1/27E $1.48, 4/27E $0.34, 7/27E $0.39. The 10/26 quarter is shown at $0.26.
risk_factors: GS upside risks to its Sell: (1) the new strategy delivers financial benefits faster than expected; (2) sales rise as consumers connect with the brand, producing share gains; (3) more newness and innovation; (4) easier competition; (5) higher margins if top-line trends accelerate.
Downside factors GS cites: pressured traffic, a tougher consumer environment, intense competition in body care, Canadian tariffs, higher crude oil costs, and buying and occupancy deleverage.
Brand sentiment among younger consumers will take time to improve.

tension_points.bull_case: 3Q sales beat consensus ($1,577mn vs. $1,551mn) and the y/y decline narrowed to -1.1% from -2.3%. New franchises (Essentials, Everyday Luxuries, Reserve) show strong repeat and growth. Ulta expands to ~1,500 stores and Amazon is winning back share.
tension_points.bear_case: Traffic remains pressured, body care is well below expectations with HSD declines, and 4Q guidance (-5.5% to -2.0%) is at the low end with a below-expectations bottom line. Tariffs and oil add over 100bps and ~100bps of gross margin pressure. GS does not expect a return to growth this year.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS names upside risks: strategy benefits arriving faster than expected, market share gains, higher newness, easing competition, or higher margins from faster top-line trends.

theme_stances.key_argument: The company is in an investment year and the underlying business remains under pressure, so it is too early to signal an inflection.
theme_stances.evidence: too early to signal an inflection in the overall business
